title: Chat status
description: What the connector reports about one chat (contract 06 C-06.24). Contract 05 carries it as a message body; contract 07 owns how the hub orders and catches up on these (seq, boot). Every field is derived from host reads the connector makes over loopback through lib/client, with no X-WC-Remote, no Origin and no Sec-Fetch-* header, never through the relay (C-06.28): GET /api/health (lib/server/routes/health.js), GET /api/queue/policy (lib/server/routes/queue.js), GET /api/asks (lib/server/routes/asks.js), the registry's MCP presence rows (lib/util/registry.js mcpSessionsFor) and the retain stream's graph events (lib/server/routes/events.js). It carries counts, states and times only: no prompt text, no lock message, no path of an owned root (contract 11).

chat_id.description: The chat this is about, by its label (contract 03 section 2).

rev.description: The assignment rev the connector has applied (0: none yet).

boot.description: The connector process's boot token, opaque to the hub (contract 07 treats boot tokens so); today pid:start-ms, the daemon's bus bootId shape (lib/server/index.js). A new boot restarts seq.

seq.description: Per connector boot, increasing across all chats. The hub keeps the newest per chat.

at.description: When the connector composed this status, epoch ms.

state.description: preparing: cloning, making a space or running init; starting: daemon spawned, identity not yet confirmed; running: daemon confirmed and held; stopping: hold released or shutdown sent; stopped: no daemon; refused: the assignment cannot be applied (see reason); failed: it was tried and did not work (see reason).

reason.description: Why the state is refused or failed, or why a wanted session is not running (cap, paused, home-launch-off, no-tmux, needs-trust, no-claude). needs-trust: connector mode is wanted but no manual `connect attach` has run in this root yet (a registry MCP row does not count), so a launched session would stop at Claude Code's workspace trust dialog (C-06.26). clone-failed also covers a ref refused before git ran (C-06.16).

detail.description: One sentence for the machine page. Never a path under workdir, never prompt text.

daemon.description: The chat's daemon, from GET /api/health; null when none answers.

up.description: A daemon answers as this root's instance.

package_version.description: health.package_version: the web-chat release the daemon runs.

boot.description: health.boot: the daemon's per-boot id; a change means it restarted.

viewers.description: health.viewers: open /ws sockets, local and relayed. The connector's own hold is not one.

viewer_peers.description: health.viewer_peers (getViewerSummary, lib/server/ws.js; sent at the local level only, connector branch; Q-06.13): open sockets split by peer, so the machine page can tell a local viewer from a relayed one before a `now` stop. Null when the daemon predates the field.

local.description: Sockets from a local, unrelayed browser.

remote.description: Sockets relayed by the connector or the portal.

started_by.description: connector: this connector spawned it and handed it the relay secret (C-06.19). other: a daemon it adopted, on any root (the user's `claude-web-chat open`, or an MCP auto-spawn after a manual attach, an owned root included); the hub shows the chat as waiting for a restart until the connector's idle restart (a C-06.22 shutdown followed by a spawn) makes it a connector daemon. stop_mode now and disconnect shut down connector daemons and any daemon on an owned root (C-06.22); an other daemon on an offered folder is only released.

held.description: The connector's retain stream is open on it.

mirror_enabled.description: health.mirror.enabled: false when a marker file turned the chat's surface off on the machine (10 C-10.5a). The connector reports it and never removes a marker.

session.description: The Claude Code session(s) attached to the chat root, from the registry's role:'mcp' rows and GET /api/queue/policy, plus the connector's own tmux probe for `attach` (C-06.24, A-06.1). Non-null whenever an MCP presence row names the root or the probe finds the launched tmux session (then `attached` may be false and `count` 0: a launch window, or a Claude Code that has not loaded its MCP server), so a live session is never reported as none; null when neither.

attached.description: At least one live MCP presence row names this root.

channel.description: GET /api/queue/policy channel_connected: a Push wakes Claude now instead of parking.

mod.description: GET /api/queue/policy mod_attached (ctx.bridge.any(), lib/server/domain/bridge.js; new on the connector branch, Q-06.6): the web-chat mod is attached (the composer's submit path). Null when the daemon's policy does not carry the field.

launched_by.description: connector: launched by this connector under tmux (web-chat's tmux launcher, C-06.26); user: started by hand or with `connect attach`. With connector, `attach` names the multiplexer session (amendment A-06.1).

attach.description: The multiplexer session a terminal can attach to (amendment A-06.1, C-06.26): non-null only when launched_by is connector and `tmux has-session -t '=<name>'` (the exact-match target) answers at the status tick (C-06.24), with or without an MCP presence row; null in manual mode (the user's own tmux, if any, is not the connector's to name), when the launched session is gone, or when tmux is absent. A connector from this amendment on MUST send it (null included); the schema leaves it optional so a status from an earlier build and the locked examples stay valid. The hub reads the name from here and never composes it; 10's GetChatAttach serves it as `session` (C-10.14a, A-10.1), the same object.

multiplexer.description: The multiplexer the launcher used. tmux in v1.1; another value (zellij) is an amendment.

name.description: The session name as the launcher created it: wc-<chat-label> and nothing else (C-06.26, ruled SW2), so the pattern is `wc-` and contract 03's chat label; tmux keeps neither `.` nor `:` in a name and the pattern admits neither, and every character is inside 10 C-10.14a's safe set. The project's display path rides the session option @swc_project, not the name.

package_versions.description: The web-chat releases the attached MCP servers run (registry sessions() package_versions).

last_tool_at.description: Latest tool call any attached session made (registry last_tool_at).

attach.description: A manual session (launched_by user, or none named) reports no multiplexer session (A-06.1).

turn.description: The graph's turn lock, from GET /api/health and the graph turn-begin / turn-end / unlock events.

in_flight.description: health.lock is set and health.lock_stale is false.

author.description: health.lock.author: a typed prompt, a channel-woken turn, or a task.

needs_you.description: What waits on the user, from GET /api/asks as a host read, the read 05's status poll makes (counts only).

asks.description: Open permission prompts, questions and plans.

count.description: queue_count: items waiting for a Push.

over_cap.description: True when this chat's session is one more than the effective cap allows (a manual session the connector could not prevent).
